pair.english: Do you have your ID card?
I want to withdraw some cash.
How much is the transfer fee?

lessons.culture: At a Gulf bank you show your ID card (the Emirates ID in the UAE, the civil ID in Kuwait) and the clerk asks you to sign. Money in general is "فلوس", cash is "كاش", and a friendly "يعطيك العافية" to the clerk is normal.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I want to withdraw some cash."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; the Gulf says "أبي" and "كاش".

exercises.tip: "أبي" is I want; "كاش" is cash. Some speakers say "أبغى".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I want to exchange some dollars."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; "أصرف" is the everyday word for changing money.

exercises.tip: "أصرف" and "أبدل" both mean to change money; "شوي" is a little or some.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where's the ATM?"?
exercises.tip: "الصراف الآلي" is the ATM; "وين" is where.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where do I sign?"?
exercises.tip: "أوقع" is I sign; the clerk answers "هني، على الخط".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "التحويل؟ / بكم / رسوم".
exercises.tip: "بكم" asks the price; "رسوم" are fees.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "هالمبلغ / في / حسابي / أبي / أحط".
exercises.tip: "أحط" is I put; here it means to pay money into an account.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أبي أسحب _____" English meaning: I want to withdraw some cash.
exercises.tip: "فلوس" works too when you mean money in general.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بكم رسوم _____؟" English meaning: How much is the transfer fee?
exercises.tip: "التحويل" is the transfer; "رسوم" is fees.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "عندك البطاقة؟". Reply: yes, here is my card.
exercises.tip: "إي" is the Gulf yes.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "بكم رسوم التحويل؟". Reply: five dinars.
exercises.tip: "دنانير" is dinars, the money of Kuwait.

lessons.culture: In the Gulf a postal address is often a PO box number (ص.ب) plus a landmark, since people find a house by a landmark more than by a street number. Private courier companies are also popular for parcels sent abroad.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I want to send a parcel to my country."

too_formal.item: أريد أن أرسل طرداً إلى بلدي
too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; speech says "أبي أرسل طرد".

exercises.tip: "طرد" is a parcel; "بلدي" is my country.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I want a stamp, please."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; speech says "لو سمحت".

exercises.tip: "لو سمحت" is please; to a woman say "لو سمحتي".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where's the mailbox?"?
exercises.tip: "صندوق البريد" is the mailbox; "مكتب البريد" is the post office.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Has my parcel arrived?"?
exercises.tip: "وصل" is arrived; the question needs only a rising voice.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "هني / اكتب / العنوان".
exercises.tip: "اكتب" is the command to a man; to a woman say "اكتبي".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الشحن؟ / بكم".
exercises.tip: "بكم" asks the price; "الشحن" is the shipping.

exercises.tip: "طرد" is a parcel; a letter is "خطاب".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بكم _____؟" English meaning: How much is the shipping?
exercises.tip: "الشحن" is the shipping cost.

exercises.tip: "أسبوعين" is two weeks; "يمكن" is maybe.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "وصل طردي؟". Reply: one moment, I will check.
exercises.tip: "بشوف" is I will see, with "ب" for the future.

pair.english: Does this phone take two SIM cards?
I want to top up my balance.

response.english: How much do you want to add?

lessons.culture: You register a SIM card with your ID or passport at a phone shop, and internet comes as monthly packages (باقات). Phone shops also sell chargers and covers and repair screens.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I want to buy a SIM card."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; speech says "أبي أشتري شريحة".

exercises.tip: "شريحة" is a SIM card; some people also say "خط" for a line.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I want to top up my balance."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; speech says "أعبي رصيد".

exercises.tip: "أعبي" is I fill; "رصيد" is the balance.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "I want a new charger."?
exercises.tip: "شاحن" is the charger; "جديد" is new.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "How long is it valid?"?
exercises.tip: "مدة" is the period; the answer is a number of days.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مكسورة / شاشة / تلفوني".
exercises.tip: "الشاشة" is the screen; "مكسورة" is broken.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "إنترنت / أبي / باقة".
exercises.tip: "باقة" is a package or bundle.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أبي أعبي _____" English meaning: I want to top up my balance.
exercises.tip: "رصيد" is the balance on your phone.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شاشة تلفوني _____" English meaning: My phone screen is broken.
exercises.tip: "مكسورة" is broken; the screen is feminine.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "بكم هالباقة؟". Reply: ten dinars a month.
exercises.tip: "في الشهر" and "بالشهر" both mean a month.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تقدرون تفعلون الخدمة اليوم؟". Reply: yes, within an hour.
exercises.tip: "إي" is yes; "خلال ساعة" is within an hour.

lessons.culture: In the UAE the police number is 999, the ambulance 998 and civil defence (fire) 997; in Kuwait one number, 112, reaches the police, ambulance and fire service. Say where you are first, speak slowly, and stay on the line.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "Call an ambulance."
exercises.tip: "اتصل" is the command to a man; to a woman say "اتصلي".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "I need a doctor."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but formal; speech says "أبي دكتور".

exercises.tip: "دكتور" and the older "دخطر" are both heard in the Gulf.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "There is a fire."?
exercises.tip: "فيه" means there is.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where is the nearest hospital?"?
exercises.tip: "أقرب" is nearest.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "سمحت / عجل / لو".
exercises.tip: "عجل" is hurry up; to a woman say "عجلي".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "عربي / زين / ما / أتكلم".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شنو رقم _____؟" English meaning: What is the emergency number?

exercises.tip: "إحنا" is we.

response.english: We will take you to the hospital.

pair.english: I want a report from the police.

lessons.culture: After an accident the police usually write a report (تقرير) that the insurance company asks for, and nobody should move an injured person. To someone who has come through safely you say "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى السَّلَامَة", fixed wording that is the same in every dialect.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "There has been an accident."
exercises.tip: "صار" is happened; "حادث" is an accident.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "My leg hurts."

too_formal.feedback: Written style; "عور" is the everyday verb for hurting.

exercises.tip: "عور" is the Gulf verb for hurt; "رجلي" is my leg.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Bring the first aid kit."?
exercises.tip: "جيب" is bring; "علبة الإسعافات" is the first aid kit.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Do not move."?
exercises.tip: "لا" before the verb forbids; to a woman say "لا تتحركين".

exercises.prompt: You hear: "أنا زين، الحمد لله". Reply: thank Allah for your safety.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "جيب علبة الإسعافات". Reply: here it is.
exercises.tip: "هذي" is here it is, said of something feminine; "علبة" is feminine.

reply.english: Don't mention it, it's our duty.

response.english: Don't mention it, it's our duty.

lessons.culture: In a mall or a market, go straight to a security guard or the information desk, and they will announce it on the loudspeaker. Keep a recent photo of your child on your phone, and be ready to say his age and what he is wearing.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "My child is lost."
exercises.tip: "ولد" is a boy or a child; for a girl say "بنتي ضايعة".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Gulf Arabic: "He is five years old."

too_formal.feedback: Formal; the Gulf says "سنين" for years.

exercises.tip: "سنين" is the Gulf plural for years.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where is the information desk?"?

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where did you see him last?"?

exercises.prompt: You hear: "لقيناه!". Reply: thank Allah!

challenge.title: A morning of errands
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Gulf Arabic. In it you withdraw cash at the bank, ask where the post office is and what sending a parcel costs, and top up your phone balance. Be polite, and use at least one sentence spoken to a woman.
required_elements: a request at the bank such as أبي أسحب كاش
a question about where a place is with وين
a question about a price with بكم
a request to top up the phone balance such as أبي أعبي رصيد
a sentence spoken to a woman such as كم تبين؟
a polite word such as لو سمحت or مشكور
